newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money trades steady, mkt eyes Buba.
newsitem.headline: German call money trades steady, mkt eyes Buba.

text.p: German call money traded steady at 3.03/05 percent on Thursday in calm trading conditions with dealers looking for the Bundesbank to hold interest rates steady but saying a change in reserve policies may be made.
By now Wednesday's seemingly generous 7.9 billion mark net injection into the money market has proven to be just enough to keep call money rates steady, dealers said.

Already on Wednesday they said the move had no policy implications. Today the market expects the central bank to hold key interest rates steady. But there is increased talk the Bundesbank will exempt repos from minimum reserve requirements.

German commercial banks have long lobbied the Bundesbank to free repos from the reserve requirement as it is widely seen as a burden which has prompted banks to shift their repurchase business in German securities from Frankfurt to London.
Bundesbank sources said the topic has been discussed for some time, and a decision should be reached soon.

Such a step however would not mean Germany has abandoned its concept of holding minimum reserves, which it deems as an important measure to guide monetary policy. Rather it would be seen as part of the central bank's drive to reform reserve policies to make Germany a more attractive financial centre.
Dealers said however that an expemption of the repo business would not dramatically affect the money market.
For today, dealers said there is ample liquidity allowing rates to trade steady around current levels.

Banks reserves at the Bundesbank totalled 42.8 billion marks on Wednesday after 37.6 billion marks on Tuesday. The monthly average was 39.9 billion marks compared with 39.0 billion marks one day earlier. Lombard borrowings stood at 100 million marks on Wednesday compared with 200 million one day earlier. The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was set at 3.07517 percent on Thursday after 3.06567 percent.
